text:
lina: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (prefer AVX2 kernels for short sequences) I'm seeing a slow but steady KV residency growth for tenant alpha when we hit long-context workloads (~12k tokens). Not sure if it's retention or fragmentation.

tom: Ugh. Any pprof/alloc traces?

lina: grabbing heap pprof now. Saw this in staging:

```
pprof: top 20 alloc_space
1. runtime.mSpanAlloc  42%  
2. github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Page).Keep  18%
3. bytes.makeSlice  12%
```

ana: Could be longctx keeping KV pages alive in the prefix cache. Did the kernel change also adjust batching heuristics?

lina: Yes — batching now groups by seq_len bucket aggressively which increased average batch size. That reduced token cost but might extend KV lifespan because requests hold references longer in the worker.

meya: @lina can you dump per-tenant KV residency histogram? want to see noisy neighbor effect.

lina: posted histograms to S3. Quick summary: tenant alpha has a right-shifted residency distribution — median page residency ~45s vs global median 12s. Also fragmentation metric (free slabs per page) is ~2x baseline.

derek: Sounds like a mix of long-lived refs + slab fragmentation. If one tenant holds many sparse longctx keys we get underutilized slabs and slower reuse.

ana: Two options: tighten per-tenant soft quota or evict policy for pages with low reuse score. We risk hurting tail lat for alpha.

lina: Agreed. I ran a simulation with proportional quota bump and a small early-evict penalty for low reuse pages. Result: overall fairness improved but alpha saw 3% increase in 95p latency.

meya: Can we do adaptive eviction: rate-limit evictions per-tenant so heavy tenants don't thrash others but also allow opportunistic reclamation when global free pool low?

lina: Prototype policy: incremental victim_score = base_score + frag_bonus - reuse_decay; then if tenant_quota_exceeded prefer victims from that tenant with extra penalty. Pseudocode: 

```
for page in candidate_pages:
  score = base_score(page)
  if page.frag > FRAG_THRESH: score += FRAG_PENALTY
  score -= reuse_half_life(page)
  score += tenant_over_quota(page.tenant) ? OVER_QUOTA_BONUS : 0
select min(score)
```

tom: Nice. Do we have telemetry to validate? need: per-tenant residency, evict rate, reuse_after_eviction, latency delta.

lina: I've added metrics: kv.residency_ms.p50/p95 by tenant, kv.evicts/sec by tenant, kv.reuse_post_evict_ratio. Pushed to dashboard under eng-runtime -> kv-isolation.

sre-bot: deploy:kv-evict-policy v0.1 rolled to canary (node group canary-3).

meya: Let's canary with two knobs: (A) OVER_QUOTA_BONUS=15 (aggressive), (B) OVER_QUOTA_BONUS=5 (mild). Run each 30m and compare: fairness (Gini on residency) and alpha 95p latency.

lina: Running A now on canary-3. I'll collect metrics and post a short summary.

ana: Also keep an eye on fragmentation compaction — maybe add a background slab compactor triggered when free-slab-ratio < 0.2. That might avoid hurting tenants when we evict.

lina: Good call. I'll prototype compactor but keep it low priority for the canary run.

meya: If compaction looks heavy, add a rate limiter and only compact slabs with >X% unused.

lina: Update after 30m: aggressive policy dropped global residency p95 by 22% and improved reuse_post_evict_ratio by +8%. Alpha 95p latency increased 4.5% (higher than sim).

derek: 4.5% is rough but maybe acceptable if unit-cost improves. What's cost delta?

lina: Token-cost/unit decreased ~3.2% on canary due to better reuse in middle tenants.

meya: We should try mild policy next — if mild gives 15% residency drop with <1% latency hit for alpha that's ideal.

lina: Switching to OVER_QUOTA_BONUS=5. Will run 30m then post numbers.

tom: Also let's add a regression test: create synthetic longctx tenant that simulates alpha and ensure eviction policy doesn't regress reuse.

lina: On it. I'll add a small loadtest in infra/benchmarks/kv_longctx_tenant and wire into CI-nightly.

meya: Thanks all. Next steps: 1) finish mild canary run 2) evaluate compactor impact 3) add synthetic test + move mild policy to more nodes if metrics look ok. Tagging @derek for /cc on implementation details. :thumbsup:

lina: thanks everyone — will post final numbers in ~2h.
